stem: Sovereignty means

options.A: the supreme power of the state to make and enforce laws

explanationCorrect: Sovereignty is the supreme, final legal authority of the state within its territory.

explanationsWrong.B: The right to vote is franchise (suffrage).
explanationsWrong.C: That's judicial independence, one principle of democracy.
explanationsWrong.D: Majority rule is a feature of democracy, not sovereignty.

stem: The word 'democracy' comes from Greek words meaning
explanationCorrect: Demos (people) + kratos (rule/power) = rule by the people.

explanationsWrong.A: Rule by the rich is plutocracy.
explanationsWrong.B: Rule by the few is oligarchy.
explanationsWrong.C: Rule by God (or religious leaders) is theocracy.

stem: The theory of separation of powers is most associated with
explanationCorrect: Montesquieu, in The Spirit of the Laws (1748), argued that legislative, executive and judicial powers should be separate.

explanationsWrong.A: Dicey is associated with the rule of law.
explanationsWrong.B: Marx is associated with communism and class struggle.
explanationsWrong.D: Hobbes is associated with social contract theory and absolute sovereignty.

stem: The concept of the rule of law was popularised by
explanationCorrect: A. V. Dicey set out the rule of law: supremacy of law, equality before the law, and rights protected by courts.

explanationsWrong.A: Montesquieu is known for separation of powers.
explanationsWrong.C: Locke wrote on natural rights and limited government.
explanationsWrong.D: Rousseau wrote on the general will.

stem: In a federal system of government, powers are

options.A: shared between the central and component units by the constitution
options.C: held by the component units, which can leave at will

explanationCorrect: Federalism divides powers between central and regional/state governments, guaranteed by a written constitution.

explanationsWrong.D: Military rule isn't a structure of federalism.

stem: In a parliamentary system, the head of government is the
explanationCorrect: The prime minister leads the government; the head of state is often a monarch or ceremonial president.

explanationsWrong.A: In a presidential system the president is head of both state and government.
explanationsWrong.B: The chief justice heads the judiciary.
explanationsWrong.C: The speaker presides over the legislature.

stem: A rigid constitution is one that

options.B: can be amended by a simple majority
options.C: requires a special procedure to amend

explanationCorrect: Rigid constitutions need special procedures (e.g. two-thirds majority, state approval) to change.

explanationsWrong.A: Rigidity is about amendment, not whether it's written.
explanationsWrong.B: Amendment by simple majority describes a flexible constitution.
explanationsWrong.D: A bill of rights has nothing to do with rigidity.

stem: Pressure groups differ from political parties mainly because pressure groups

options.B: seek to influence policy, not to form government

explanationCorrect: Pressure groups influence government decisions but don't seek to control government through elections.

explanationsWrong.C: Contesting elections is what parties do.
explanationsWrong.D: Pressure groups are legal and common in democracies.

stem: Franchise refers to
explanationCorrect: Franchise (suffrage) is the right to vote in elections.

explanationsWrong.B: That's the commercial meaning, not the political one.
explanationsWrong.C: The number of parties describes the party system.

stem: Which of these is a feature of the civil service?
explanationCorrect: Civil servants are anonymous, neutral and permanent; ministers take public responsibility.

explanationsWrong.A: Civil servants are expected to be politically neutral.
explanationsWrong.B: Civil servants are appointed, not elected.

stem: In the pre-colonial Oyo empire, the body that checked the powers of the Alaafin was the
explanationCorrect: The Oyomesi (council of seven, led by the Bashorun) could check the Alaafin and even ask him to commit suicide.

explanationsWrong.A: The Ogboni was a secret society that checked the Oyomesi.
explanationsWrong.B: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo was the military commander.
explanationsWrong.D: Emirs ruled in the Hausa-Fulani system.

stem: The traditional Igbo political system is best described as
explanationCorrect: Most Igbo communities had no single ruler; authority was shared among elders, age grades and assemblies.

explanationsWrong.A: Centralised systems describe Hausa-Fulani and Oyo.
explanationsWrong.C: Most Igbo communities had no king.
explanationsWrong.D: Religion played a part, but it wasn't rule by priests.

stem: Indirect rule in Nigeria is most associated with
explanationCorrect: Lugard used traditional rulers to govern on behalf of the British, first in Northern Nigeria.

explanationsWrong.B: Clifford is associated with the 1922 constitution.
explanationsWrong.C: Richards is associated with the 1946 constitution.
explanationsWrong.D: Macpherson is associated with the 1951 constitution.

stem: The first political party in Nigeria, the NNDP (1923), was founded by
explanationCorrect: Herbert Macaulay founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party in 1923.

stem: Which constitution introduced the elective principle in Nigeria?
explanationCorrect: The 1922 Clifford Constitution allowed elected members from Lagos and Calabar to the Legislative Council.

stem: Nigeria became a republic in
explanationCorrect: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963, replacing the British monarch with a Nigerian president as head of state.

explanationsWrong.A: 1960 was independence, but the Queen remained head of state.

stem: Nigeria's first military coup took place on
explanationCorrect: The first coup was on 15 January 1966, ending the First Republic.

explanationsWrong.C: 29 July 1975 was the coup that removed Gowon.

stem: ECOWAS was established in
explanationCorrect: ECOWAS was set up by the Treaty of Lagos on 28 May 1975.

explanationsWrong.A: 1963 was when the OAU was founded.
explanationsWrong.B: 1999 is when Nigeria returned to civil rule.
explanationsWrong.C: 2002 is when the African Union replaced the OAU.

stem: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was replaced by the African Union in
explanationCorrect: The African Union was launched in 2002 in Durban, South Africa.

explanationsWrong.A: 1963 is when the OAU itself was founded.
explanationsWrong.D: The AU had already existed for eight years by 2010.

stem: The centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy has traditionally been
explanationCorrect: Since independence, Africa has been described as the centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy (decolonisation, ECOWAS, peacekeeping).

explanationsWrong.A: Europe is a major partner but not the centrepiece.
explanationsWrong.C: Asia is a growing partner but not the stated focus.
explanationsWrong.D: The Americas aren't the centrepiece either.
